mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST falls >10% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines >0.5% for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent rise in the Consumer Price Index above 4% signals monetary policy lag and inflationary pressure, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.33% (4% annualized)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL > 4% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth > 2% month-over-month for three months) alongside a simultaneous decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1 flat or falling) signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces demand and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 2% for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 monthly change <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS grows >2% for three months and GDPC1 is flat/falling.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in a high-inflation environment.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY
regime_hint: high inflation with tight labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS grows >0.5% for three months and CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 5% for four consecutive months signals a robust recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts materials, homebuilding, and related equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises >5% for four consecutive months.
